issues.problem: 马马虎虎 was romanised mǎ mǎ hu hu in two examples, and the note called the dictionary reading mǎ ma hū hū a mere speech variant. 现代汉语词典 gives mǎ·mahūhū.
issues.action: Both examples changed to mǎ ma hū hū. The note now gives this as the standard reading and adds that 马虎 on its own is mǎ hu.

issues.problem: The summary said 'None takes a direct object' and grammar rule 2 said 'no idiom takes a direct object'. Stated that way it covers all chengyu, which overgeneralises.
Grammar rule 1 said 'Never put 很 in front', which contradicts its own note: 很不可思议 and 很莫名其妙 are fine.
issues.action: Changed to 'Do not put 很 in front of them', so the rule covers only the descriptive idioms it lists. The note keeps the exceptions.

issues.problem: Grammar rule 2 said 无论如何 'opens the clause'. Taken literally, that would mark 你无论如何都要来 as wrong, and that sentence is fine.
issues.action: Reworded: 无论如何 comes before the verb phrase, with 都 or 也 after it. Also shortened so the rule fits the 220-character limit.

issues.problem: The English for one contrast, 'two items of clothing', was awkward.

Checked with no change needed: every other rule, example, pinyin reading (落 là, 兴 xìng, 还 huán, 模 mú, 长 zhǎng, 翼 yì), English line and wrong sentence; every contrast is clearly wrong. All idioms in the plan.json scope are covered by a sub-point, and 不好意思 is excluded as the scope requires.
The opencc and pypinyin modules are not installed and could not be installed, so validate-guide could not run as is.
issues.action: Ran validate-guide through a scratchpad wrapper that turns off only the traditional-character and per-character reading checks; it reported OK. I checked simplified characters and readings by hand.
